expect: ~7 million metric tons of reserves x ~70% mining efficiency x ~40% directed to batteries = ~2 million metric tons (p1.L42-47, Fig. 1 caption)
question: How does the review get from the known global cobalt reserves to the cobalt usable for batteries, and what amount results?
rendered:
The review assumes a conservative ≈70% yearly mining efficiency with ≈40% of the mined cobalt directed toward battery manufacturing. 

If the known global cobalt reserves are ≈7 million metric tons, then the total usable battery-specific cobalt from the total reserves is ≈7 * 0.4 * 0.7 = ≈2 million metric tons.
